searchText: Used MultiFaucet to send you Goerli ETH: https://faucet.paradigm.xyz/ Hi, I haven't followed on all the testing that is being done financed by the EF. I'm interested in one particular line of testing and I'd like to know if this is being carried out or not before I set on the task of doing it. I would want to create a network fork without finalization for a couple of days, stop a node wait a few hours and relaunch it. That is, I want to test if a node that has the latest finalized point in db plus a few forks but possibly missing some justified points, can sync from the network. I'm worried that we've made many changes since this code was actually needed in runtime and we haven't been testing this at scale, and these are the sort of things that are only urgent when you need them. Perhaps <@219015859182632960> has been testing this? Any idea why Ethereumjs has only 55 tests instead of 110 like the other engines on https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/? Timeouts There are individual timeouts per test as well as an overall timeout Oh see. Makes sense thanks. Hello. That’d need to be added but would be easy to add. We are splitting a network so it stops finalizing, wait a couple days, then rejoin it. Stopping a node for a few hours and then letting it rejoin the network, before joining the network as a whole again, would be an easy addition. Thanks, I'd like to know if prysm breaks under this, there have been a lot of changes lately, and init sync is a pain in the butt Yeah cool. Copy/pasted that in the thread where we are discussing the next testing round. Is the testing call happening and in the usual place (zoom is empty)? hello, i have a question about LatestValidHash, so what is it actually? is it the latest valid block we received from CL or the latest head (maybe not confirmed by fcu)? It's the latest valid ancestor of the block that we are currently processing e.g. in a chain p1 <- p2 <- p_inv <- p3 <- p4, the LVH for p4 would be p2 got it 👍 another thing, is it fine for returning a void hash on ACCEPTED in case we do not have any reconnection to the chain Yes I think null is the expected response in that case One aspect I've noticed is that I've never seen an LVH in cases where the CL sends `p4`, which isn't ready yet (so, one of `SYNCING`/`ACCEPTED` depending on details, but it's caught up with `p2` in an optimistic sync, so it might be able to tell the CL that, well, it's partly caught up. so as an EL gradually state-syncs, it might be able to respond with more and more recent LVHes Being optimistic has a cost for a CL -- it can't really finalize anything yet, which is a major mechanism/trigger for clearing old states from needing to be accessible, for example. wait what do you mean here by the CL not being able to finalize? we can certainly finalize being optimistic and **we will prune** everything from forkchoice once we have finalized, optimistic or not, and some clients will even remove from db the older, non-finalized (therefore orphaned) blocks, optimistic or not, valid or invalid. Does https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/specification.md#payload-validation or some other part of the specs provide enough assurance that `INVALID` can't crop up later, e.g., that either a block is immediately marked invalid or it's never invalid? We can finalize an INVALID block, I'm not denying that. But that will require 2/3 of the validators to vote on an INVALID block We have larger problems in that case than pruning being optimistic okay, in which case, at least that's what I was getting at with "can't". But sure, it's at least internally consistent. Finalization is purely a consensus concept and does not involve execution in anyway more than honest validators could not have voted for a block being optimistic
